_comment: directoryOrder exists for dependency ordering. The nine type tables are mutually independent —
no seeded row in one references a row in another — so any order would apply cleanly today. They
are listed anyway, because the ordering becomes load-bearing the moment pipelines are seeded:
Pipeline references DealType and ForecastCategoryType, and PipelineStage references
DealStatusType and ForecastCategoryType. Establishing the list now means adding pipelines later
is one line rather than a debugging session.
DealType.DefaultPipelineID is deliberately left NULL in the seeds. It is the other half of the
DealType <-> Pipeline cycle, and seeding it would require pipelines to exist first — which they
cannot, since a Pipeline needs a real __mj.Company. Pipelines are per-deployment data, not
vocabulary, so they are not seeded here at all.
_comment_remote_operations: remote-operation-categories MUST precede remote-operations: the operation rows resolve their
CategoryID with @lookup against a category by Name, so the category has to exist first. This is
the first entry in this list where the ordering is genuinely load-bearing rather than
precautionary — get it wrong and the push fails on an unresolvable lookup.
_comment_entity_relationships: entity-relationships is the odd one out: it does not seed rows at all. It fills in one column on
three EntityRelationship rows CodeGen already created, turning them into typed writable child
collections on Deal. It is listed last because it depends on nothing, and because reading it last
matches when it matters — CodeGen pass 2 is what consumes it. See its README.
